newsitem.title: CANADA: Bre-X drops on investor confusion.
newsitem.headline: Bre-X drops on investor confusion.

text.p: Shares in Bre-X Minerals Ltd dropped on Friday morning as confused investors tried to figure out seemingly contradictory details of Bre-X's new deal to develop the Busang gold deposit in Indonesia.
Bre-X fell C$1.50 to C$21.20 in trading of more than 2.8 million shares in the first two hours of trading. The drop was a reversal of Thursday's trading, which saw the stock jump C$1.20.
"It's beginning to look a lot like a dog's breakfast," said one trader.
Analysts said market players were confused about statements Bre-X officials made earlier this week about selling its stake in the Busang deposit.

Bre-X chief executive David Walsh told a conference call of media and analysts on Monday that its partners in Busang -- two Indonesian companies and Freeport-McMoRan Copper and Gold Inc -- do not have rights of first refusal if Bre-X receives a third-party offer.
But Indonesian businessman Muhammad "Bob" Hasan, who controls the two Indonesian companies, contradicted Walsh in an interview with the Toronto Globe and Mail on Friday.

Hasan said Bre-X must consult with its Busang partners because the rights of first refusal are "part of the usual articles of (business) incorporation in the Republic of Indonesia," the Globe reported.
The contradiction prompted a sell-off of the stock, analysts said. Bre-X would not immediately return calls.
Bre-X was also asked by the Toronto Stock Exchange and the Ontario Securities Commission to clear up confusion about its stake in the Busang deposit.

Bre-X had always maintained it controlled 90 percent of the deposit before its deal with Freeport. But during the conference call this week, Bre-X said shareholders were mistaken to believe it owned 90 percent.
Early Friday, Bre-X released a statement saying it had indeed held 90 percent of the property before its joint venture deal with Freeport.

Bre-X said it agreed on February 17 to drop its holding to 45 percent "in order to satisfy the national interest of the people of Indonesia, to ensure the expeditious development of the Busang gold project."
"I just shake my head," said analyst Michael Jalonen at Midland-Walwyn.
